verdicts.tldr: urlOf(r) is evaluated three times per realm in one loop body; one local removes two calls for one added line
verdicts.details: Read at head: shots.go:72 head.FileOf(urlOf(r)), :76 slug(strings.TrimPrefix(urlOf(r), "/")), :89 base.FileOf(urlOf(r)) — three evaluations of the same expression per realm, all on the same r. urlOf (crawl.go:470) is strings.Cut plus a concat and is pure, so the after shot, the slug and the before shot cannot disagree today: the divergence the candidate describes is latent, not a live defect, which is why this is a readability win and not a bug. The minimal hoist is gofmt-clean and the package still passes. Fix: bind u := urlOf(r) above the head.FileOf call and read u at all three sites.

verdicts.verify_by: go doc os/exec.LookPath for the slash rule, then in a scratch dir: touch chromium && chmod -x chromium, and call findChrome("") with CHROME unset from that working directory; observe a non-empty return whose exec fails | read shots.go:195-212: LookPath is the executability test and the Stat fallback has no IsExecutable check; confirm with touch /tmp/x && gnopreview render -chrome /tmp/x
verdicts.tldr: the os.Stat fallback hands back a browser path that cannot be executed, so a clean skip becomes one exec failure per page
verdicts.details: exec.LookPath resolves a slash-carrying path directly whenever it is runnable, so the -chrome flag, $CHROME and the macOS bundle path all reach the caller through the LookPath branch at shots.go:205. The os.Stat branch at :208 therefore fires only when the path exists, is not a directory, and LookPath refused it — no exec permission. findChrome returns it, bin != "", and every chromeShot then dies with permission denied, printing '  ! screenshot <url>: ...' once per page instead of the single '  ! no Chrome/Chromium found' line at :53 and :119. A bare name is worse: os.Stat resolves "chromium" against the working directory while exec.Command re-resolves a separator-free name on PATH, so the value returned cannot be run at all, even when the cwd file is executable. What the user loses is the diagnosis, not the preview — screenshots are best-effort and both routes end with no images. Fix: drop the os.Stat branch, or gate it on the executable bit and on the candidate carrying a path separator.
verdicts.evidence: Wrote judge-75-findchrome-stat-fallback_test.go into misc/gnopreview in a scratch worktree at ecf7af0f2 and ran go test -run TestJudge75 -v. All three pass at head. TestJudge75_LookPathCoversExecutableSlashedPath: a 0755 file named 'Google Chrome' comes back from exec.LookPath unchanged, so Stat is never consulted for a runnable candidate. TestJudge75_StatFallbackReturnsNonExecutable, same file at 0644: 'LookPath rejected it: exec: "/tmp/.../chrome-no-x": permission denied', findChrome still returns that path, and 'every chromeShot on this bin fails: fork/exec /tmp/.../chrome-no-x: permission denied'. TestJudge75_StatFallbackReturnsBareNameUnrunnable, PATH set to an empty dir, CHROME empty, cwd holding an executable ./chromium: findChrome returns "chromium" and 'exec.Command re-resolves it on PATH and fails: exec: "chromium": executable file not found in $PATH'.

verdicts.tldr: base is the serve() origin string at line 122 and the merge-base *Crawler at line 50, in one file
verdicts.details: shots.go:50 declares func ScreenshotPairs(outDir string, head, base *Crawler, ...) and calls base.FileOf; :122 binds srv, base, err := serve(outDir) and uses base+"/"+p.File as an HTTP origin. Same identifier, two types, seventy lines apart, in two functions that share the whole findChrome -> serve -> MkdirAll prologue — the obvious place for a later edit to move a line. The sibling already spells it origin at :56, so the file disagrees with itself. Nothing misbehaves today; the cost is the next reader and the next edit. Fix: rename the Screenshot local to origin, matching ScreenshotPairs.
